correctness.rationale: The four-point Fourier coefficients on each orbit separate the lifted measurements by j−k modulo four. The diagonal polynomial vanishes at 1, 2, 3, giving a line. In the complex first harmonic, the three equations have an invertible Vandermonde submatrix on the first three unknowns, leaving a complex line. The two aligned squares force the real parts in the second harmonic to vanish, and the middle square gives the remaining real relation, leaving a real line. An independently authored exact calculation using all twelve sites and a real Hermitian basis reproduced rank 12, the four-parameter kernel, the principal-minor coefficient determinant 6064128 and the c=0 determinant polynomial. Rank at most two implies all four principal minors of order three vanish, so invertibility forces c³=0. At c=0 the determinant is 1089(a²+b²)²+11520a²b²+132(a²+b²)t²+4t⁴, which vanishes only at zero. A difference of rank-one lifts has rank at most two, so equality of intensities implies equality up to phase, including the zero polynomial. Compactness of the Hermitian rank-at-most-two unit Frobenius sphere gives the asserted uniform stability bound.
residual_risks: The optimal stability constant and measurement-count minimality are not established or claimed.
